name: 热带雨林
era: 赤道两侧 · 终年高温多雨
oneLiner: 物种最丰富的陆地生态系统，分层结构复杂，是地球的碳汇与生物多样性热点。
oneLinerEn: The most species-rich terrestrial ecosystem, with layered structure—Earth's carbon sink and biodiversity hotspot.

positions.v: 亚马逊、刚果、东南亚
乔木层 / 林下层 / 地被
占全球一半以上陆地物种

why: 固碳、调节气候、提供药物与基因资源；其消失会放大全球变暖与物种灭绝。
whyEn: Stores carbon, stabilizes climate, supplies medicines; its loss amplifies warming and extinction.

name: 珊瑚礁
era: 浅海热带 · 清澈温暖
oneLiner: 珊瑚虫与虫黄藻共生建成的海底结构，单位面积生物多样性最高的生态系统之一。
oneLinerEn: Structures built by corals and their algal symbionts—among the most biodiverse ecosystems per area.

positions.v: 珊瑚虫 × 虫黄藻共生
热带大陆架与环礁
庇护幼鱼、防波护岸

why: 支撑渔业与海岸防护；对海水升温敏感，白化事件频发警示海洋健康。
whyEn: Supports fisheries and coastal protection; heat-driven bleaching signals ocean health.

name: 温带落叶林
oneLiner: 以冬季落叶的阔叶乔木为主，季节变化明显，是重要的碳库与木材来源。
oneLinerEn: Dominantly winter-deciduous broadleaves with strong seasons; a key carbon stock and timber source.

positions.v: 东亚、北美东部、欧洲
positions.vEn: E Asia, E N America, Europe

positions.v: 落叶适应低温
碳储存与木材

why: 调节水文与碳循环，为大量鸟类与哺乳动物提供栖息地。
whyEn: Buffers water and carbon cycles and shelters many birds and mammals.

name: 草原
oneLiner: 以草本植物为主、树木稀疏的生态系统，支撑大型草食动物与捕食者，土壤肥沃。
oneLinerEn: Herb-dominated, tree-sparse ecosystems supporting large grazers and predators on fertile soils.

positions.v: 北美、欧亚、非洲 savanna
火与食草维持
农牧与碳土

why: 全球重要粮仓与牧场，土壤有机碳储量巨大，但对开垦与干旱敏感。
whyEn: Major breadbasket and rangeland with huge soil carbon, yet sensitive to plowing and drought.

name: 荒漠
oneLiner: 年降水量极低的生态系统，生物以耐旱适应（肉质、CAM 光合、夜行）生存，生态脆弱。
oneLinerEn: Ecosystems with minimal rainfall where life survives via succulence, CAM photosynthesis and nocturnality—ecologically fragile.

positions.v: 副热带高压带与雨影区
CAM 光合、肉质储水
恢复极慢

why: 提醒水资源约束；荒漠化扩张威胁生计，但物种演化出惊人适应。
whyEn: Highlights water limits; desertification threatens livelihoods, yet species show astonishing adaptation.

name: 苔原
era: 极地 / 高山 · 低温
oneLiner: 低温、生长季短、地下为永久冻土的生态系统，植被低矮，却封存着巨量有机碳。
oneLinerEn: Cold, short-season ecosystems over permafrost with low vegetation that lock away enormous organic carbon.

positions.v: 北极圈与高山带
永久冻土
冻土融化释碳

why: 冻土碳库对气候反馈敏感，融化可能加速变暖，是气候临界点之一。
whyEn: Its frozen carbon is climate-sensitive; thawing could accelerate warming—a tipping point.

name: 深海
oneLiner: 阳光无法到达、高压低温的海洋底层与热液口，生命依靠化能合成而非光合作用。
oneLinerEn: Sunless, high-pressure, cold ocean depths and vents where life runs on chemosynthesis, not sunlight.

positions.v: 化能合成（热液 / 冷泉）
海沟、洋中脊、平原
生命起源候选地

why: 占地球宜居体积大部分，可能藏着生命起源线索与未知物种。
whyEn: Most of Earth's habitable volume; may hold origin-of-life clues and unknown species.

name: 湿地
era: 水陆交错 · 周期淹没
oneLiner: 介于陆地与水域之间的生态系统（沼泽、红树林、河口），净化水质、蓄洪并养育候鸟。
oneLinerEn: Ecosystems between land and water (marshes, mangroves, estuaries) that clean water, buffer floods and feed migratory birds.

positions.v: 沼泽 / 红树林 / 河口
净化与蓄洪
候鸟驿站与渔场

why: 单位面积固碳能力极强，却因填海造地消失最快，保护优先级高。
whyEn: Among the highest carbon sinks yet disappearing fastest to land reclamation—high protection priority.

name: 红树林
era: 热带与亚热带的潮间带泥滩
eraEn: Intertidal mudflats of the tropics and subtropics
oneLiner: 生长在咸淡水交汇潮间带的耐盐木本植物群落，是海岸的天然屏障与育幼场。
oneLinerEn: Salt-tolerant woody plants on the intertidal where fresh meets sea — a natural coastal shield and nursery.

positions.v: 支柱根、呼吸根与排盐机制应对缺氧高盐。
positions.vEn: Stilt and air roots plus salt excretion cope with low oxygen and salinity.

positions.v: 种子在母树萌发成胚轴后落地生根。
positions.vEn: Seeds germinate on the parent into propagules before dropping.

why: 消浪护岸、固碳储泥，并为鱼虾蟹与候鸟提供庇护，是高效的蓝色碳汇。
whyEn: Damps waves, shields coasts, buries carbon and shelters fish, crabs and migratory birds — a potent blue-carbon sink.

name: 深海热液喷口
eraEn: Lightless deep sea along mid-ocean ridges
oneLiner: 海底热泉喷出矿物与化学能，化能合成细菌支撑起不依赖阳光的独特生命绿洲。
oneLinerEn: Superheated mineral springs whose chemosynthetic bacteria power oases of life independent of sunlight.

positions.v: 以硫化氢等化学能替代光合作用。
positions.vEn: Chemical energy from hydrogen sulfide replaces photosynthesis.

positions.v: 管虫、盲虾与嗜热微生物成群聚集。
positions.vEn: Tube worms, eyeless shrimp and thermophiles cluster densely.

why: 重新定义了生命的能量边界，也是探索地球生命起源与地外生命的钥匙。
whyEn: Redefines the energy limits of life and offers clues to life's origin and to possible life beyond Earth.

name: 海藻林
oneLiner: 大型褐藻（海藻）构建的水下森林，生长极快，是近海生物多样性最高的生境之一。
oneLinerEn: Underwater forests of giant brown algae — among the fastest-growing and most biodiverse near-shore habitats.

positions.v: 固着器、柄与叶片随波摇曳形成三层。
positions.vEn: Holdfast, stipe and blades sway in layered canopy.

positions.v: 海獭捕食海胆，间接守护海藻林。
positions.vEn: Sea otters eat urchins, indirectly guarding the kelp.

why: 提供栖息与饵料、固碳并支撑渔业；海胆暴增与升温易使其崩解为荒芜。
whyEn: Shelters life, feeds fisheries and stores carbon; urchin blooms and warming can collapse it into barrens.

name: 热带稀树草原
era: 雨林与荒漠之间的热带地带
eraEn: Tropical belt between rainforest and desert
oneLiner: 以禾草为主、散生乔灌的开阔生态系统，干湿季交替并依赖周期性的自然火。
oneLinerEn: Open grassland dotted with trees, driven by wet–dry seasons and periodic fire.

positions.v: 自然与人为火维持草本优势、抑制林木。
positions.vEn: Natural and human fire keeps grass dominant and checks trees.

positions.v: 大规模有蹄类与迁徙塑造植被格局。
positions.vEn: Mass ungulate herds and migrations shape the vegetation.

why: 孕育地球上最壮观的野生动物迁徙与捕食者—猎物共演化，也支撑牧业文明。
whyEn: Hosts Earth's grandest wildlife migrations and predator–prey coevolution, and underpins pastoral cultures.

name: 潮间带
era: 海陆交界的周期性涨落带
eraEn: The heaving boundary between sea and land
oneLiner: 随潮汐在海水与空气间轮换的狭窄地带，生物须同时耐受干旱、冲击与盐度波动。
oneLinerEn: A narrow strip alternating between submerged and exposed, where life must endure drying, wave shock and salinity swings.

positions.v: 不同耐受带的物种呈垂直分层分布。
positions.vEn: Species with different tolerances form vertical bands.

positions.v: 固着、闭壳与黏附对抗脱水与浪击。
positions.vEn: Attachment, clamping and gluing resist drying and waves.

why: 物质与能量在海洋和陆地间交换的枢纽，也是研究生态位与竞争的经典舞台。
whyEn: A hub of sea–land exchange and a classic stage for studying niches and competition.

name: 岛屿生态系统
era: 海洋与湖泊中的孤立陆地
eraEn: Isolated land in oceans and lakes
oneLiner: 与大陆隔绝的岛屿催生独特的适应辐射与高特有率，也格外脆弱于入侵与灭绝。
oneLinerEn: Isolation breeds unique adaptive radiations and high endemism — and makes islands unusually vulnerable to invasion and extinction.

positions.v: 祖先种分化出占据不同生态位的众多后代。
positions.vEn: A founder splits into many species filling different niches.

positions.v: 常出现巨化、矮化与失飞等现象。
positions.vEn: Gigantism, dwarfism and flightlessness are common.

why: 达尔文雀与马达加斯加生物是演化论的摇篮；岛屿物种占当前灭绝危机的大头。
whyEn: Darwin's finches and Madagascar cradled evolutionary theory; island species dominate today's extinction crisis.

name: 泥炭地
era: 寒冷湿润的沼泽与苔原
oneLiner: 未完全分解的植物残体经千年累积成泥炭，是单位面积储碳最高的陆地生态系统。
oneLinerEn: Partly decayed plant matter accumulates as peat over millennia — the densest carbon store per area on land.

positions.v: 长期积水缺氧使有机物分解极慢。
positions.vEn: Waterlogging and low oxygen slow decay to a crawl.

positions.v: 面积虽小，却封存全球约三成土壤碳。
positions.vEn: Small in area yet holds roughly a third of soil carbon.

why: 关键的天然碳库与蓄水层；一旦排水或燃烧会把巨量碳迅速释回大气。
whyEn: A vital carbon vault and water reservoir; draining or burning it releases vast carbon fast.
